seasonal_note: Apples, winter squash, and Brussels sprouts are at their best around Portland this week.

meals.name: Grilled Chicken Thighs with Charred Broccolini
meals.description: Smoky, mild thighs the kids will eat; extra thighs feed Monday's bowls.
ingredients: 4 lb boneless chicken thighs (half reserved for Monday)
recipe_steps: Whisk oil, lemon juice, and garlic; marinate the chicken overnight.
Heat the grill to medium-high.
Grill thighs 5-6 min per side until they reach 165F inside.
Grill broccolini 3-4 min until lightly charred.
Refrigerate half the chicken for Monday.

meals.name: Greek Chicken Bowls
meals.description: Uses Sunday's extra chicken over cauliflower rice.
recipe_steps: Saute cauliflower rice 6-8 min.
Slice the chicken and warm it in the same pan.
Chop cucumber and tomatoes.
Assemble bowls and top with tzatziki.

meals.name: Slow Cooker Pork Carnitas Lettuce Wraps
meals.prep_note: Start the slow cooker at 8am on LOW.
meals.description: Mild carnitas in butter lettuce cups.
recipe_steps: Season the pork with cumin and salt.
Add pork and orange juice to the slow cooker; cook on LOW 8 hours.
Shred and crisp the pork under the broiler 4-5 min.
Serve in lettuce cups with pico.

meals.name: Sheet Pan Sausage and Squash
meals.description: One pan, seasonal squash, minimal cleanup.
recipe_steps: Heat the oven to 425F.
Cube the squash and halve the sprouts; toss with oil and salt.
Roast 15 min, add sliced sausage, roast 15 min more until the sausage reaches 165F.

meals.name: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
meals.description: Quick weeknight stir-fry with a mild sauce.
recipe_steps: Slice the steak thinly against the grain.
Sear the steak in batches 2 min per side; set aside.
Stir-fry the broccoli 4 min, add sauce and the steak, toss 1 min.

meals.name: Turkey Burger Lettuce Wraps
recipe_steps: Form four patties and season.
Grill 5-6 min per side until they reach 165F inside.
Serve wrapped in lettuce with tomato and cheddar.

budget_tips: Chicken thighs anchor two dinners this week.
A 3 lb pork shoulder at Costco is cheaper per pound than smaller packs.
pantry_note: Assumes salt, pepper, dried spices, and cooking oil on hand.
